name: Trans fatty acids
aliases: trans fats, trans fatty acids, partially hydrogenated oil, partially hydrogenated vegetable oil, iTFAs, grasas trans
what_is: Trans fats are unsaturated fats from two sources. Some occur naturally in meat and dairy from ruminants. Industrial trans fats are made mainly by partially hydrogenating oils.
why_botia: High trans-fat intake raises LDL cholesterol and is associated with a higher risk of coronary heart disease and death. That evidence does not show a greater risk in women or prove hormonal disruption.
can_1: Detect 'partially hydrogenated' oils or explicit 'trans fat' declarations on labels.
can_2: Explain the cardiovascular evidence and, when the label allows it, whether the source is industrial or natural.
cannot_1: Measure the exact amount of trans fats in the food if it is below standard regulatory disclosure thresholds.
cannot_2: Determine if naturally occurring trans fats from dairy or meat are present versus industrial ones.

sources.label: WHO Plan to Eliminate Industrially-Produced Trans-Fatty Acids (REPLACE)

title: Trans fatty acids
description: Unsaturated industrial fats created by partially hydrogenating vegetable oils to make them solid at room temperature.
